page.layout: One page of text in a single column. In the left margin, beside the line "pronio fecisse, tum Titius da", a small illegible mark. Running head at the top with the page number 114.

main_text.p: » cidit. Agit is,cui manus præ- » cisa est,iniuriarum. Postulat » is, qui cum agitur à, prætore » exceptionem,Extra quam in » reum capitis præiudicium fiat. » Hic is qui agit, iudicium pu- » rum in hæc uerba postulat: » Si paret Titiū iniuriam Sem » pronio fecisse, tum Titius da » mnetur. Ille qui cum agitur, [illegible, ~3 letters]nimirum Titius, exceptio- nem addi ait oportere,Extra quam in reum capitis præ- iudicium fiat. Intentio: Pu- rum iudicium dandum est. Depulsio: Imò cum excep- tione. Quæstio: Excipien- dum fit, necne. R. Non e- nim oportet in recuperato-rio

page.notes: The line-initial » marks are printed on every line of the text and are transcribed as printed. The left-margin mark beside "Titius da mnetur" is a small illegible ornament or reference mark and is not read. The running head at the top is a heavy black decorative line and could not be read. The final word "recuperato-rio" continues onto the last line, right-aligned, and is transcribed with its printed hyphen. The small marks at the foot of the page are stray specks and are left out. The long s is transcribed as plain s throughout.
